title: Linux task_struct (process descriptor)
summary: The Linux task_struct is the process descriptor, containing all information about a process/thread. Key fields: state (running, sleeping, stopped, zombie), pid (process ID), tgid (thread group ID), comm (command name, 16 chars), mm (memory descriptor), files (file descriptor table), fs (filesystem info), signal (signal handlers), sched (scheduling info: priority, policy, CPU affinity), parent (parent task), children (list of children), sibling (sibling in parent's children list), thread (thread-specific data), cred (credentials: uid, gid, capabilities), ns (namespaces: pid, net, mount, uts, ipc, user, cgroup, time).

structure.meaning: Task state: TASK_RUNNING, TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE, TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE, TASK_STOPPED, TASK_TRACED, EXIT_ZOMBIE, EXIT_DEAD.
Process ID (thread ID in kernel terms).
Command name (executable name, truncated to 15 chars + NUL).
Memory descriptor: VMAs, page tables, mmap, brk, etc.
Scheduling info: priority, vruntime, CPU affinity, load weight.
Credentials: uid, gid, euid, egid, capabilities, securebits.
Namespaces: pid, net, mount, uts, ipc, user, cgroup, time.
Thread-specific: CPU registers, FPU state, TLS, etc.

notes: task_struct is ~6-8KB in size (varies by kernel config).
task_struct is allocated from the slab allocator (or kmalloc).
The kernel uses a doubly-linked list (tasks) to traverse all processes.
The scheduler uses the sched_entity for fair scheduling (CFS: Completely Fair Scheduler).
